l: Simple riverine lakes are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish present (e.g., panfish and some bass or northern pike). Water tends to flow though these lakes quickly (on average less than 15 day residence-time) and they tend to be small in surface area - many of these are small millponds on warmwater streams. There are 175 simple riverine lakes in Wisconsin, scattered across all parts of the state.
Simple riverine lakes may have good action opportunities for smallmouth bass and quality opportunities for northern pike. They rarely have any walleye or muskellunge.

Simple warm dark lakes are characterized by simple fish communities, typically with fewer than 4 different groups of sportfish (e.g., panfish and some bass or northern pike). Water temperatures tend to be warmer than average, and water is less clear than average. They tend to be small in surface area.  This is the most common class of lake in Wisconsin, with 1,650 simple warm dark lakes  scattered across all parts of the state.
Simple warm dark lakes can provide great opportunities for action for black crappie, and often also support bluegill and largemouth bass. They rarely have any walleye or muskellunge.
